                    ### Question
                    In a 68-year-old patient with new onset headache, pain and prolonged morning stiffness in scapular and pelvic girdles of several weeks of evolution that presents unilateral bruising of sudden onset, what treatment among the following would establish before confirming the diagnosis?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Prednisone 10 mg daily v.o.
opb. Methylprednisolone 1 g i.v. daily for three days.
opc. Cyclophosphamide i.v. 1 g / m2.
opd. Infliximab i.v. 3 mg / Kg.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In a 68-year-old patient with new onset headache, pain, prolonged morning stiffness in scapular and pelvic girdles, and unilateral bruising, prednisone 10 mg daily v.o. should be initiated before confirming the diagnosis. This is supported by the rapid improvement in symptoms seen with prednisone. Methylprednisolone 1 g i.v. daily for three days may offer faster onset of action compared to oral prednisone but is not the initial treatment choice. Cyclophosphamide and infliximab are reserved for specific conditions like severe lupus nephritis and refractory rheumatoid arthritis, respectively, and are not indicated as first-line treatments in this case.
